issue.body:
### Verify canary release

- [X] I verified that the issue exists in the latest Next.js canary release

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
      Platform: darwin
      Arch: arm64
      Version: Darwin Kernel Version 22.3.0: Mon Jan 30 20:38:37 PST 2023; root:xnu-8792.81.3~2/RELEASE_ARM64_T6000
    Binaries:
      Node: 16.19.1
      npm: 8.19.3
      Yarn: 1.22.19
      pnpm: 7.3.0
    Relevant packages:
      next: 13.3.5-canary.12
      eslint-config-next: 13.4.0
      react: 18.2.0
      react-dom: 18.2.0
```


### Which area(s) of Next.js are affected? (leave empty if unsure)

App directory (appDir: true), Routing (next/router, next/navigation, next/link)

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/brunocangs/next-app-parallel-issue

### To Reproduce

Run the project with `yarn dev` and navigate to `http://localhost:3000`

### Describe the Bug

When using Parallel Routes (e.g. `/app/@slot/page.tsx`), the `@slot`'s `loading.tsx` states are never called or displayed.

The current beahviours observed even differ in `dev` and `prod`, as seen in the videos references.

**Prod Link: https://next-app-parallel-issue.vercel.app/**

Dev behaviour:
- Layout displays:
  - First slot (`@slot/page.tsx`) is async, so it displays a loading state. However this is the page's loading state, not the slot loading state.
  - Second slot is not async, so it immediately displays. The Suspended component displays it's loading state correctly
- Suspended component on second slots loads
- Eventually First slot loads and displays it's suspended component correctly.
- Suspended component on first slot loads

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30100875/236318280-294f6a0f-1809-4756-bdd1-da1ca7f2d792.mov

Prod behaviour:

- Everything gets server loaded and awaited. The parts that would require basic suspending get optimized and no loading states are displayed.

I didn't include a prod video as it would only be a page reload

### Expected Behavior

It is expected that, as mentioned in the documentation, the loading state for each of the slots will be correctly displayed per the image below
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30100875/236316511-29695ff0-4051-4fe9-b565-7a8be44f5302.png)


### Which browser are you using? (if relevant)

Chrome

### How are you deploying your application? (if relevant)

Vercel

body:
So currently the parallel routes have a lot of bugs and there are still a lot of issues pending for the Next.js team to focus on, I went ahead and resolved this issue using `router.push()` and `router.refresh()` methods.

I know they will be solved soon, but releasing such big features without proper testing seems less professional. Considering I discovered this bug while toying with Next.js.

Anyhow, I'll keep this issue open until someone from the team presents a resolution!

Hi there - thanks for the report. 

Slots do not support layout files -- that shouldn't be working in dev, so we'll take a look! Parallel routes are meant to be used within a shared layout.

Our [Parallel Routes docs](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/parallel-routes) clarify this a bit more. The supported file types for a slot are `error`, `loading`, `page`, and `default`.

Hi @ztanner.

Thanks for the response! We would like to explicitly mention this in the docs as well.

Moreover, I am following the discussion https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/54075. Please correct me if I am wrong:

As of now, there is no way to always load the latest data (in my case - a new random number at every request) when we are navigating back and forth between dynamic pages (`export const revalidate = 0`) due to [Router cache](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/caching#opting-out-3). We have to explicitly call the `router.refresh()` if we want to achieve this.

I am asking this because we are considering using Next.js as our framework for building new upcoming commercial products.
Our business requirements include NOT showing any stale data.

Thanks in advance!

Hi @jainmohit2001 - yes indeed, I'll dig into the slot `layout` case a bit more, and we'll make sure to update the documentation based on the results from that.

Regarding caching, your understanding is correct. For dynamic segments, there's a 30s router cache. `router.refresh()` will purge the router cache and force a request to the server. There's a proposal for a `staletime` property (read more [here](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/54075#discussioncomment-6754339)) which will let you explicitly override the defaults to bypass the 30s heuristic.

Thanks a lot for your quick response @ztanner. 

The `staletime` proposal seems to address our requirements. Looking forward to that!
 
Closing this issue as `layout.tsx` is not supposed to be used with parallel route Slots.

issue.title: parallel routes: support multi-slot layouts
issue.body:
### What?
When using layouts in multiple parallel route slots, only 1 of the layouts would render.

### Why?
The `resolveParallelSegments` logic responsible for populating the loader tree was incorrectly bailing if it found another parallel route that matched a page component. 

### How?
I did my best to update this loader code with some more comments to make it a bit easier to reason about, and also made some slight refactors. But the gist of the fix is just ensuring that each parallel route (that isn't a direct match on the `children` slot) is resolved as an array, so that when the subtree is created, it doesn't skip over the slot.

Fixes #58506
Fixes #59463

Closes NEXT-2222

body: Hey @jainmohit2001 , just to follow-up, it turns out we did intend to support multiple layouts in parallel slots and I've fixed it in #61115
This closed issue has been automatically locked because it had no new activity for 2 weeks. If you are running into a similar issue, please create a new issue with the steps to reproduce. Thank you.
